summary: Add GET /api/alerts/trends?days=N (default 7, min 1, max 90) returning one bucket per UTC calendar day for the last N days (oldest first), each with a total count and per-severity counts, with zero-filled days/severities and 400 ValidationProblemDetails on invalid days.

acceptance_criteria.text: GET /api/alerts/trends with no days parameter returns 7 daily buckets (default); days=N within [1,90] returns N buckets.
Buckets are one per UTC calendar day covering the last N days, ordered oldest day first.
Each bucket includes its UTC day, a total alert-creation count, and a count per severity (Low, Medium, High, Critical).
Days with no alerts, and severities with no alerts within a day, appear with explicit zero counts (no missing days or severities).
Per-severity ordering/naming reuses the existing summary severity convention (Severity enum order Low to Critical).
Invalid days (below 1, above 90, or non-numeric) returns 400 with ValidationProblemDetails, consistent with existing query-parameter validation.

scope_anchors: AlertManagementService trend aggregation + zero-fill assembly (mirrors GetSummaryAsync)
IAlertRepository daily-count aggregation over AlertDbContext.Alerts grouped by UTC date
New AlertTrendQueryRequest with [Range(1,90)] days validation (mirrors AlertQueryRequest)
adjacent_dependencies: AlertService.API/Program.cs (TimeProvider DI already registered; no change expected)
constraints: Compute 'today'/now in UTC via the injected TimeProvider, never DateTime.UtcNow directly, matching existing service code.
Bucket by UTC calendar date of Alert.CreatedDate (stored UTC); each bucket represents one whole UTC day.
Keep AlertsController HTTP-only; do trend aggregation + zero-fill in the service; keep the raw grouped query in the repository, matching existing layering.
Zero-fill every UTC day in the requested range and every severity so all days/severities are present even with no alerts.

Validate days via DataAnnotations [Range(1,90)] on a bound query request type (default 7), mirroring AlertQueryRequest so invalid/out-of-range/non-numeric input yields ValidationProblemDetails automatically under [ApiController].
Reuse the existing AlertSeverityCountsResponse shape for per-bucket severity counts; add new response types only for the trend envelope and per-day bucket.
No database schema or migration change is required.
coverage_goals: Behavior coverage for the trend endpoint: default 7 days; explicit valid days; oldest-first ordering; total and per-severity counts; zero-filled empty days/severities; days=1 and days=90 boundaries accepted; days=0, days=91, and non-numeric rejected with 400 ValidationProblemDetails.
unresolved_questions: Non-blocking (resolve in /implement-story): confirm the trend day-count constants (default 7, min 1, max 90) are added to AlertConstants, and decide whether daily grouping is done in SQL (GroupBy on CreatedDate.Date) with zero-fill in the service, or counts pulled and bucketed in the service. Recommended: SQL groups by UTC date, service zero-fills the full range and every severity.
